subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should first-party iOS Siri/App Intent execution be added, and if so should it use paired-node identity, chat.send/node.event, or a hardened /hooks/agent boundary with what confirmation, session, and spoken-reply policy?
rationale: The implementation is feasible, but it creates a new voice/Shortcuts agent-execution surface where auth, session routing, confirmation, reply collection, and spoken output are product and security decisions.

options.title: Approve design-gated native intent
options.body: Implement the Siri/App Intent only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.

options.title: Limit scope to Talk Mode launch
options.body: Allow first-party shortcuts only for opening Talk Mode while leaving dictated questions and spoken agent replies out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep webhook workaround external
options.body: Decline first-party Siri agent execution for now and keep Shortcuts plus webhook as the supported power-user workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve design-gated native intent
recommendation.body: Implement the Siri/App Intent only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.
